claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is equiatomic.
The as-synthesized catalyst has a random atomic distribution.
The as-synthesized catalyst has no significant surface enrichment of any element.
Electrochemical potential cycling between 0.2 and 1.2 V vs. RHE drives Ru migration to the catalyst surface.
Surface-segregated Ru undergoes partial oxidation during potential cycling.
Potential cycling produces nanoscale, surface-localized Ru-rich domains that are partially oxidized to RuO2.
RuO2 surface domains activate water at lower overpotentials.
Water activation at RuO2 domains generates adsorbed OH species.
Adsorbed OH species oxidatively remove poisoning intermediates such as CO or acetate from neighboring active sites.
The relevant regenerated active sites are primarily Pt sites.
Removal of poisoning intermediates regenerates active sites and sustains catalytic performance.
Compared with an untreated catalyst, the potential-cycled catalyst will show slower catalytic-current decay during ethanol oxidation.
Compared with an untreated catalyst, the potential-cycled catalyst will show a higher peak current density.
Compared with an untreated catalyst, the potential-cycled catalyst will produce a higher fraction of complete ethanol-oxidation products such as CO2.
XPS or STEM-EDS will reveal greater surface Ru concentration after potential-cycling pretreatment.
Surface characterization will reveal RuO2 signatures after potential-cycling pretreatment.
The proposed mechanism should hold in 0.5 M H2SO4 containing 1.0 M ethanol at 20–80 °C when pretreatment cycles span 0.2–1.2 V vs. RHE.
The mechanism is analogous to behavior in PtRu catalysts and to beneficial effects of surface oxides on catalytic regeneration.

contradictions.description: Activity and selectivity effects are described as only potential and quantitatively uncertain, but the falsification rule rejects the entire durability-centered hypothesis if peak activity or complete-oxidation selectivity does not improve.
